name: Shimea
overview: Shimea is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified as the son of Michael. He is associated with the Gershonite family line, descendants of Gershon, son of Levi, which situates him within the Levitical clan responsible for specific religious duties. His lineage underscores his role within the Levitical priestly heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimea means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name that conveys attentiveness or submission. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:39 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly states that Shimea is the son of Michael (1 Chronicles 6:40), and it is inferred that Berechiah is his father (1 Chronicles 6:39). Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the scriptural record.
scriptureSignificance: Shimea's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, specifically among the Gershonites, who carried out important duties in the tabernacle service. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:39-40 highlights the continuity of priestly service through his lineage, emphasizing God's providential preservation of the Levitical order. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, Shimea represents the faithful transmission of religious responsibilities within Israel's covenant community.
